text: I am comparing Q’s learning-augmented contract for fallible semantic predictions with P’s LMM comparison/rank-aggregation/reward-shaping pipeline. I will check whether P’s theoretical guarantee actually controls prediction error, query cost, or changing agent sets, and look for a precise theorem or counterexample connecting the papers.

Q is a survey of prediction interfaces and formal consistency/robustness; P uses LMM pairwise comparisons, Bradley--Terry scores, and potential reward shaping in cooperative MARL. I am testing whether Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s prediction-error/cost framework yields a concrete robustness or query-allocation result for P, while checking P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s assumptions before claiming any transfer.

Concrete obstruction in P: §Method (lines 283–330) queries each ordered active pair and fits unregularized Bradley–Terry MLE; Proposition 1 (lines 363–377) assumes only connected comparison graph for a finite \(O(\sqrt{n\log n/K})\) error bound. For \(n=2\), two comparisons of the sole pair make the graph connected, yet if both outcomes favor agent 1 the likelihood is maximized only as \(c_1-c_2\to+\infty\). Under a true BT tie \(c_1^*=c_2^*\), this happens with probability \(1/4\) (and either unanimous direction with probability \(1/2\)); so an unregularized finite MLE does not exist on half of samples, contradicting the stated \(1-n^{-2}=3/4\) high-probability assertion. P’s appendix proof silently needs bounded scores/regularization and graph spectral/sample conditions, not mere connectivity. Q’s §Semantic Predictions and §Pricing the Prediction make this a testable interface/cost question rather than an LMM calibration claim.

Potential key distinction: P (Potential Function, lines 331--348) defines \(F_t=\gamma\psi_{t+1}-\psi_t\) with terminal \(\psi=0\). For a complete episode, \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^t F_t=-\psi_0+\gamma^T\psi_T=-\psi_0\), pathwise. Thus score error at intermediate steps changes the training signal but not the exact discounted objective for a fixed initial potential; P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s rank-estimation proposition alone does not imply better final return. Q (Inference Graphs, lines 1023--1110; Pricing the Prediction, lines 1242--1258) explicitly requires edge sensitivity and query cost. I am checking active-agent bookkeeping and whether the P estimator premise is actually sufficient.

Cross-check of ada #3: with two active agents and two independent ordered BT draws at a true tie, unanimous outcomes have probability \(1/2\); connectedness holds but the unregularized MLE diverges. Separate bridge: under P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s terminal-zero PBRS, for each agent \(G_i^{\rm shape}=G^{\rm env}-\rho\psi_i(s_0,0)\). Hence exact \(Q_i^{\rm shape}=Q^{\rm env}-\rho\psi_i\), \(V_i^{\rm shape}=V^{\rm env}-\rho\psi_i\), and \(A_i^{\rm shape}=A^{\rm env}\) when the critic conditions on the full potential state. If the critic is represented as \(\widetilde V_i=\widehat V_i^{\rm env}-\rho\psi_i\), its TD residual equals the unshaped TD residual exactly. P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s experimental learning gains therefore require finite-sample/function-approximation/credit-routing effects; neither BT score consistency nor pairwise accuracy alone explains them. This is a distinct Q-to-P inference-graph edge to test.

Sharpening the cross-paper question: Q §Evaluation Criteria defines guarantees on downstream cost, while P §Potential Function (lines 331–349) uses \(F_{i,t}=\gamma\psi_{i,t+1}-\psi_{i,t}\). If each agent has a fixed-coordinate potential through entry/exit, all transitions are credited, and terminal potential is zero, then pathwise \(\sum_{t=0}^{T-1}\gamma^tF_{i,t}=-\psi_{i,0}\), regardless of comparison errors. Thus exact policy ordering is prediction-independent; P’s observed benefit after finite MAPPO training must be a learning-dynamics/compute effect. Its softmax also has \(\sum_i\psi_{i,t}=1\) at each nonterminal nonempty coalition, so total team shaping is independent of rank scores if rewards are pooled. P §Method gives \(\psi_t\in\mathbb R^{|I^t|}\) but no explicit cross-coalition embedding or reward-credit convention; an active-only implementation can break the telescoping at reentry. Prior work already proves dynamic PBRS invariance (https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/75121/) and shows PBRS can increase policy-gradient variance (https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/a5357781c204d4412e44ed9cbcdb08d5-Paper-Conference.pdf). So a publishable target should be finite-training success or gradient variance per charged LMM query, with entry/exit handled explicitly, not a new optimal-policy invariance theorem.

Concrete Q→P research contract: measure predictor error by its effect on finite-training policy-gradient variance (or success at a fixed compute budget), and charge each ordered comparison. In a one-step frozen-policy REINFORCE model, \(z=\nabla_\theta\log\pi_\theta(a\mid h)\), \(g_b=z(G-b(h))\), \(b=\rho\psi_i\). Conditional expected gradient is unchanged and the second moment is minimized at \(b^*(h)=\mathbb E[\|z\|^2G\mid h]/\mathbb E[\|z\|^2\mid h]\), with excess \(\mathbb E[\|z\|^2\mid h](b-b^*)^2\). This defines an outcome-aligned error \(\eta_{\rm PG}\), unlike P’s pairwise rank accuracy (lines 540–548). Counterexample: two agents, agent 2 inert, \(\pi_\theta(a_1=1)=1/2\), \(G=a_1\), \(\rho=1\). Agent 1 truly contributes more (Shapley \((1/2,0)\)), so ideal BT/softmax gives \(\psi_1>1/2\). But \(b^*=1/2\), and the neutral \(b=1/2\) gives zero gradient variance while every \(\psi_1>1/2\) gives positive variance. Hence more accurate ordinal credit can hurt finite-sample learning even with perfect comparisons. This is a toy diagnostic, not a claim about MAPPO; existing work already finds that potential shaping can increase variance (https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/a5357781c204d4412e44ed9cbcdb08d5-Paper-Conference.pdf), and query-policy misalignment is known in preference RL (https://proceedings.iclr.cc/paper_files/paper/2024/hash/c703e3320a0d0f1ed2e2b95964249c17-Abstract-Conference.html). Distinct potential contribution: budgeted, validated comparisons for open-team PBRS with performance/variance per query and explicit entry/exit accounting.

I put the checked derivations and paper line citations in ada/pair_note.md. P §LMM comparison specifies a call for each ordered active pair, so its stated protocol costs \(q_t=|I^t|(|I^t|-1)\) calls per queried decision step (e.g. \(2,6,12,90\) for active sizes \(2,3,4,10\)); P Appendix Experimental Details reports 50M-step MAPPO training within 16h versus MARS-RA within 30h, without a formal success-per-call guarantee. Q §Pricing the Prediction says an objective-unit conversion \(\kappa\) must be declared. My narrow prior-work searches included `"multi-agent" "potential-based" "pairwise" reward shaping queries`, `"open" "multi-agent" potential based reward shaping changing agents`, `"Bradley-Terry" "potential-based reward shaping" multi-agent`, and `"query" "gradient variance" preference based reinforcement learning reward shaping`; results included P and adjacent dynamic PBRS / preference-query work, not a checked novelty conclusion.

Sharpened question and derivation in emmy/potential_bridge.md: Given P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s PBRS and Q\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s demand for an error-sensitive composition edge, which approximate-critic mechanism makes LMM comparisons improve final unshaped return per training query? Exact matched-critic TD and GAE residuals cancel pathwise: if \(\widetilde V_i=\widehat V_i^{\rm env}-\rho\psi_i\), then \(\delta_i^{\rm shape}=\delta_i^{\rm env}\). With critic mismatch \(e_i\), the difference is \(\gamma e_{i,t+1}-e_{i,t}\), giving a concrete downstream error channel to measure. Proposed discriminating controls: matched critic, uniform and randomized scale-matched potentials; report held-out unshaped return, advantage mismatch, critic error, query count/latency under fixed environment-step and wall-clock budgets. P lines 550--552 reports accuracy/query benefit, lines 781--783 says training rises from 16 to 30 hours; Q lines 1242--1258 motivates cost accounting. Existing potential-shaping equivalence is prior art: Wiewiora 2003 https://www.cs.cmu.edu/afs/cs.cmu.edu/project/jair/pub/volume19/wiewiora03a.pdf and Devlin--Kudenko 2012 https://aamas.csc.liv.ac.uk/Proceedings/aamas2012/papers/2C_3.pdf . Search queries are in note; no novelty claim for cancellation alone.

Cross-check of emmy #9: the matched-critic TD/GAE cancellation is correct under a single cached full-population potential and complete reward accounting. A sharper coalition boundary: even if \(\psi_{i,t}=0\) whenever \(i\notin I^t\) and terminal \(\psi_{i,T}=0\), an active-at-\(t\)-only reward mask \(a_{i,t}=1_{\{i\in I^t\}}\) leaves \(\sum_t\gamma^t a_{i,t}F_{i,t}=-a_{i,0}\psi_{i,0}+\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\gamma^t(a_{i,t-1}-a_{i,t})\psi_{i,t}\) (terminal term zero). At reentry \(a_{i,t-1}=0,a_{i,t}=1,\psi_{i,t}>0\), this adds \(-\gamma^t\psi_{i,t}\); the prior positive increment was skipped. So terminal-zero alone does not ensure invariance if only active agents receive rewards. P lines 289–306 and 331–349 never specify this mask/embedding, so this is an implementation question, not proof of an actual P bug.

Cross-check of ada #7: the one-step Bernoulli example is correct. For a logit-parameterized \(\pi(a_1=1)=1/2\), \(z=a_1-1/2\), \(G=a_1\), and a state-only baseline \(b\), \(g_b\) takes values \((1-b)/2\) and \(b/2\), so its mean is \(1/4\) and its variance is \((b-1/2)^2/4\). A perfectly rank-correct Shapley/BT potential \(b=\operatorname{softmax}_1(1/2,0)>1/2\) is worse than neutral \(b=1/2\) on this measure. This is a counterexample to treating pairwise accuracy as downstream smoothness, not to P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s empirical results. Independent prior-work check: Gupta et al., NeurIPS 2023, §3/Property 1 explicitly proves potential shaping leaves expected PG unchanged and can raise variance: https://proceedings.neurips.cc/paper_files/paper/2023/file/a5357781c204d4412e44ed9cbcdb08d5-Paper-Conference.pdf . Therefore the toy and cancellation cannot be claimed as general novelty; the candidate advance must be the validated, cost-aware open-team mechanism.

Best account from my side: The original broad transfer question should be sharpened to “Can LMM pairwise rankings improve finite-budget learning in open-team MARL after comparison calls are charged, and through which approximation channel?” Q §Evaluation Criteria (lines 257–339), §Inference Graphs (1023–1110), and §Pricing (1242–1258) require an outcome-linked error and cost. P §Method (283–349) supplies the concrete LMM→BT→softmax→PBRS pipeline, but its Proposition 1 (363–377) controls only distance to latent LMM preferences under insufficient MLE premises, while Proposition 2 (385–390) assumes rather than establishes Shapley alignment. Emmy #9’s exact matched-critic cancellation is correct; my one-step example in ada/pair_note.md shows even ideal Shapley ranking need not reduce raw policy-gradient variance, and #10 shows a possible reentry bookkeeping failure under active-only reward masking. A viable paper would define a finite-training endpoint (unshaped success/return under fixed environment steps and wall-clock or monetary budget), repair score estimation and coalition bookkeeping, then compare standard MARS-RA with matched-critic, uniform/rand potential, and query-budget controls. If those controls erase the gain, the finding is a useful mechanism/negative result; if a charged-query gain persists, analyze the residual channel. Unresolved: P’s actual reward mask and critic architecture, correlation of repeat LMM calls, empirical effect under controls, and novelty beyond cited PBRS/active-query work. No theorem of improved MARL return or novelty claim follows from Q and P alone.
ready at #12

Additional implementation fork in P §Potential Function (lines 337--349): \(\boldsymbol\psi_t=\operatorname{softmax}(\hat{\boldsymbol c}_t)\) implies \(\sum_{i\in I^t}\psi_{i,t}=1\) for each nonterminal state with an active coalition. If MAPPO pools per-agent shaped rewards before computing its common advantage, then the rank-dependent shaping sum is \(\rho[\gamma\sum_i\psi_{i,t+1}-\sum_i\psi_{i,t}]\), independent of the ranking under a full-population embedding. If it uses separate agent critics/rewards, the ranking can affect finite-sample updates even though exact advantages remain unchanged. P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s text gives a reward vector but does not specify this credit-routing detail. This is a falsifiable audit target, not an assertion about their code.

Cross-checking emmy #14 against P lines 263 and 331–349: P defines a scalar team reward \(r\) but a vector shaped reward \(\tilde{\boldsymbol r}_t=r_t+\rho F_t\), without stating MAPPO reward routing. Let \(u_t=\sum_{i\in\mathcal N}\psi_{i,t}\), with zero embedding for absent agents. A full-population pooled transition is \(\sum_iF_{i,t}=\gamma u_{t+1}-u_t\); P softmax makes \(u_t=1\) whenever the nonterminal active coalition is nonempty, so it is independent of the ranking even across coalition changes. If pooling only agents active at \(t\), then \(\sum_{i\in I^t}F_{i,t}=\gamma[1-\sum_{i\in I^{t+1}\setminus I^t}\psi_{i,t+1}]-1\) when both coalitions are nonempty and the successor is nonterminal. Rank dependence survives only through entrant scores at that boundary, precisely where the skipped transition credit can break policy invariance. With separate per-agent shaped rewards, rank may affect approximate finite-training updates; with exact matched critics the GAE residuals cancel as emmy #9 showed. This yields a concrete reward-routing audit with three cases, not evidence of which P implements.

Ada #10 is right and I corrected emmy/potential_bridge.md. A full-population potential plus zero inactive coordinates is insufficient by itself if each agent receives shaping only while active: the active-mask sum contains \(\sum_{t=1}^{T-1}\gamma^t(a_{i,t-1}-a_{i,t})\psi_{i,t}\), giving a negative reentry term. Full reward accounting on every transition (or an explicit boundary correction) is needed for the pathwise cancellation. My #14 pooled-score cancellation applies only when pooling truly includes all population coordinates; active-only pooling can retain rank effects at coalition changes. P does not specify which implementation it uses.

I added the pooled-reward calculation and routing audit to ada/pair_note.md. A central point is now conditional but sharp: for full-population pooling of P’s vector potential, \(\sum_i\psi_{i,t}=1\) makes the team shaping independent of every LMM ranking on nonterminal nonempty coalitions; with active-only pooling, entrant weights restore a ranking signal at the cost of a possible broken telescoping identity. The discriminating replication should inspect reward tensors, inactive-agent masks, and critic targets around entry/exit, then evaluate finite-budget unshaped success per query. Style checks on the note passed with only line-length warnings.
ready at #17

Best account from emmy after cross-checking ada #3, #7, #10, #15, #17: The publishable question is conditional and narrower than the original broad transfer idea: can P\(\text{\textquotesingle}\)s LMM→BT→softmax shaping improve held-out unshaped MARL return per charged comparison under finite training, and through which critic/reward-routing channel? Q §Evaluation Criteria (lines 257--344) requires downstream error, §Inference Graphs (1023--1110) requires an edge argument, and §Pricing (1242--1258) requires call cost. P §Method (281--349) supplies the pipeline and §Further Analysis (550--552) reports an accuracy/query trend, but §Theory (358--390) controls only a latent LMM preference under assumptions that fail for unregularized MLE on connected finite samples. With cached full-population potentials and complete reward accounting, exact returns and advantages telescope, so predictor quality can affect only finite-training behavior; active-only masks create an explicit reentry term and full-population pooling removes rank dependence. The decisive experiment is a reward-routing audit plus matched-critic, neutral/random-potential, and charged-query controls at fixed steps and wall-clock time. Potential shaping/variance results are prior art (Gupta et al. 2023 URL in #11), so novelty depends on this open-team cost-aware mechanism and a reproducible empirical or conditional theoretical result. Unresolved: P implementation routing and critic inputs, correlation/calibration of repeat LMM calls, finite-training outcome under controls, and whether existing work already settles this narrow setting. Derivation and citations are in emmy/potential_bridge.md.
